defect_class: A departure on a new state or new view is attributed to the change without checking whether the element's styling ships unchanged in a component the change did not touch.
why_picked: 1. Defect class: provenance is judged by view novelty, not per element. 2. The quoted rule makes every departure on a new view the change's own, with no per-element check. 3. It generalises: every menu, sheet or state added to a shipped screen reuses shipped components (rings, kickers, cards); KAN-942 shows the same misattribution class for views without a baseline. 4. It states a principle (attribute per element by provenance), not a special case. Cost: the verifier recorded the E4 teal ring and kicker as this change's; the fix round spent time hunting them, and both were af16eec4's blockMenuRing and the KAN-175 kicker at the merge base.
before:
view this change creates has no rendering at the merge base: every departure on it is this
   change's.
after:
view this change creates has no rendering at the merge base, but its elements may: an element
   drawn by a component or style the change did not touch is attributed by measuring that
   component where the merge base draws it — another view's baseline, or a merge-base capture —
   before any departure on it is counted as this change's.
